hotspots.whyItMatters: High-voltage secondary wiring for neon has its own clearance and support rules, distinct from low-voltage branch circuits.
hotspots.cite: NEON Techniques and Handling. Confirm chapter in your copy. Cross-check NEC Article 600
hotspots.trap: Running neon secondary conductors with the same clearance and support habits used for ordinary low-voltage branch wiring.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Neon transformers (or electronic power supplies) need accessible disconnects and specific mounting practices.
hotspots.cite: NEON Techniques and Handling. Confirm chapter in your copy. Cross-check NEC 600.6
hotspots.trap: Forgetting that ground-fault protection of equipment (GFPE) is now required for neon secondary circuits under the modern code, even though this 1997 handbook predates that requirement.

hotspots.whyItMatters: A hands-on safety topic distinct from electrical rules: tube breakage and mercury handling.
hotspots.cite: NEON Techniques and Handling. Confirm chapter in your copy
hotspots.trap: Treating neon tube handling as routine glass handling without the specific breakage/exposure precautions this trade actually requires.
